settings.prompt:
You check whether a question is about the rules of badminton, before a rules bot searches the official BWF rule books (the Laws of Badminton, the Instructions to Technical Officials and the Alternative Laws).
Answer true when the question asks what the rules say, allow, forbid or require: play, scoring, service, faults, lets, the court, equipment limits, officials and their duties, match conduct. It is still a rules question when it is casual, very short, misspelled, or compares badminton with another sport.
Answer false when it is not about the rules of badminton: greetings and tests, other subjects, another sport on its own, and badminton topics that are not rules: coaching and technique, training and fitness, buying or caring for equipment, players, results, rankings, records and history.
When unsure, answer true.

You check whether a question is about the rules of badminton, before a rules bot searches the official BWF rule books (the Laws of Badminton, the Instructions to Technical Officials and the Alternative Laws).
Answer true when the question asks what the rules say, allow, forbid or require: play, scoring, service, faults, lets, the court, equipment limits, officials and their duties, match conduct. It is still a rules question when it is casual, very short, misspelled, or compares badminton with another sport.
Answer false when it is not about the rules of badminton: greetings and tests, other subjects, another sport on its own, and badminton topics that are not rules: coaching and technique, training and fitness, buying or caring for equipment, players, results, rankings, records and history.
When unsure, answer true.

In a correct service, the shuttle must fly upwards from the server's racket, pass over the net, and, if not intercepted, land in the receiver's service court on or within its boundary lines [1][2]. The server and the receiver must stand within diagonally opposite service courts without touching the boundary lines of those courts [5], and some part of both feet of each must remain in contact with the court surface in a stationary position from the start of the service until the service is delivered [6]. Neither side may cause undue delay to the delivery of the service once both are ready [3], and once the backward movement of the server's racket head is complete, any delay in starting the service counts as undue delay [4]. The first forward movement of the server's racket head is the start of the service [10], and once started, the service is delivered when the shuttle is hit by the server's racket or when the server misses the shuttle in attempting to serve [11]. The server must release the shuttle without adding spin and the racket must initially hit the base of the shuttle [7], the whole shuttle must be below 1.15 metres from the court surface at the instant it is hit [8], and the racket must keep moving forwards from the start of the service until it is delivered [9]. The server shall not serve before the receiver is ready, but the receiver is considered ready if a return of the service is attempted [12][13]. If a service is not correct, it is a fault [17]. In the best-of-5-games-to-11 format, in force 2027-01-04, you change ends at the end of the third game if there is to be a fourth game [1].
Calling 'fault' to you while you are making your stroke is a deliberate distraction [1][2]. Deliberately distracting an opponent by any action such as shouting is a fault [3].

When a 'let' occurs, play since the last service does not count and the player who served last serves again, so the rally is replayed [1]. 'Let' shall be called by the umpire, or by a player if there is no umpire, to halt play [12]. It shall be a 'let' if the server serves before the receiver is ready [2][3]. It shall be a 'let' if during service the receiver and the server are both faulted [2][4]. It shall be a 'let' if after the service is returned the shuttle is caught on the net and remains suspended on its top [2][5][6], or if after passing over the net it is caught in the net [2][5][7]. It shall be a 'let' if during play the shuttle disintegrates and the base completely separates from the rest of the shuttle [2][8]. It shall be a 'let' if in the opinion of the umpire play is disrupted or a player of the opposing side is distracted by a coach [2][9]. It shall be a 'let' if a line judge is unsighted and the umpire or Instant Review System is unable to make a decision [2][10]. It shall be a 'let' if any unforeseen or accidental situation has occurred [2][11]. A shuttle coming onto the court from an adjacent court shall not automatically be considered a 'let', and a 'let' shall not be called in such circumstances if, in the opinion of the umpire, the shuttle has not obstructed or distracted the players [13][14].

For a bleeding injury like your partner's cut hand, play should be delayed until the bleeding stops, the wound is suitably dressed, or the Referee advises the Umpire otherwise [1]. The Referee must resolve the injury situation as quickly as possible and well within a few minutes so that play can be resumed or abandoned [2], no treatment causing undue delay may be given on court [3], and the Umpire times the delay caused by the injury [4]. The Umpire must try to determine the severity of the problem as quickly as possible and call the Referee onto court if necessary [9]. As for who may come on court to help, the Referee may allow a maximum of two persons on court to assist and advise the injured player and help with translation [5], and the Referee decides whether the Tournament Doctor or anyone else is required on court [7]. If the Tournament Doctor comes on court, the doctor examines the player and advises the player about the severity of the injury or sickness [8]. In fairness, the Referee must allow the opposing side the same consideration [6].

Because the court is temporarily not playable, the Umpire shall call the Referee and play shall be suspended until the court and its immediate surroundings are again suitable for play [1]. Play may also be suspended by the Referee or Umpire if warranted by a circumstance affecting playing conditions [4], and when necessitated by circumstances not within the control of the players the umpire may suspend play for such a period as the umpire considers necessary [7], while under special circumstances the Referee may instruct the umpire to suspend play [8]. When play is suspended, the Umpire shall call “Play is suspended” and note “S” on the scoring device or score-sheet, if used [2][3]. The existing score shall stand and play shall be resumed from that point [5]. When play resumes after the suspension, the Umpire shall note the duration of the suspension and ensure that the players are on the correct side of the net and in the correct service courts, then call “Are you ready?” followed by the score and “Play” [6].

The umpire shall remind your opponent that throwing sweat or otherwise contaminating the court and its immediate surroundings is unacceptable, applying Law 16.7 if necessary [1]. Under Law 16.7 the umpire administers the breach by issuing a warning to the offending side [2][3]. The umpire may fault the offending side if they have been previously warned [2][4]. The umpire may fault the offending side in cases of flagrant offence or breach [2][5]. When the umpire faults a side, they shall report the offending side immediately to the Referee, who has the power to disqualify that side from the match [6]. The Referee shall be called on court by the Umpire in case of flagrant or other misbehaviour resulting in a red card under Law 16.7 [7].

The line judge must immediately inform the Umpire by putting both hands up to cover the eyes [1]. The Umpire then makes the decision [2][3], and where the Line Judge is unsighted the Umpire shall immediately call "Out" when the shuttle lands outside the line and then call either the score or "Service over" and then the score [4][5], or call the score or "Service over" and then the score when the shuttle lands "in" [4][6]. If the Umpire or the Instant Review System is unable to make a decision, it shall be a "let" [7], and when no decision can be made a "let" shall be called unless IRS is in use, in which case it will be used to decide on the line call [8].

During the match your coach must remain seated in his designated seat and must not stand court-side, except during the permitted intervals [1]. The permitted intervals are the interval of not more than 60 seconds during each game when the leading score reaches 11 points, except in Handicap matches [2], and the interval of not more than 120 seconds between the first and second game and between the second and third game [3]. During the interval between games and after the players have changed ends, each side may be joined on the court by no more than two accredited coaches [4], but they must leave the court when the umpire calls "20 seconds" [5].

A plastic (non-feathered) shuttle must have the same measurements and weight as a feathered shuttle, which is from 4.74 to 5.50 grams [1][3]. However, because of the difference in the specific gravity and other properties of synthetic materials in comparison with feathers, a variation of up to 10 per cent shall be acceptable for a plastic shuttle [2]. For your hot and stuffy hall, modifications to the shuttle specifications may be made with the approval of the Member Association concerned, in places where atmospheric conditions due to either altitude or climate make the standard shuttle unsuitable, subject to there being no variation in the general design, speed and flight of the shuttle [4]. From whatever material the shuttle is made, the flight characteristics generally shall be similar to those produced by a natural feathered shuttle with a cork base covered by a thin layer of leather [5].
